summary: This diff adds two solid new pytest suites (tests/execute_backlog_plan_test.py, tests/plan_backlog_completion_dedup_test.py) plus realistic fixtures covering the previously-untested execute_backlog_plan.py orchestration layer (phase1+2 collapse bookkeeping, phase3/phase3b supervisor routing, phase4 wave-sequenced redispatch) and the already-partially-tested plan_backlog_completion.py dedup/classify/apply-collapse logic, including a regression test that pins down the shell=True-to-allowlist fix (grep/pytest/python3 -m pytest only, tokenized via shlex, executed with shell=False, verified with an explicit shell-metacharacter-injection test and a source-scan guard against shell=True reappearing) and a test proving the incident root cause (crediting an unrelated merged PR as proof of completion) is fixed. All 20 tests pass locally, properly monkeypatch subprocess/dispatch_core/systemd-shaped calls, never touch real ai-os/tasks or git remotes, and correctly isolate the delegated apply_verified_collapses() call from this script's own results-bookkeeping loop. The diff is purely additive (new script files, new tests, new fixtures, a read-only audit-report YAML artifact), touches no migrations/schema/auth/permission/payment/billing/rls/security paths and no .github/workflows/** files, and the previously-hardcoded 'FChecklist' org literal in execute_backlog_plan.py's gh pr list/create calls was correctly replaced with the shared GH_OWNER constant imported from plan_backlog_completion.py. No new command-injection, path-traversal, or write-path safety regressions were found relative to the already-reviewed apply_collapse()/apply_representative_completion() guards (refuse-unless-verified-category, refuse-empty-evidence).
issues: tests/execute_backlog_plan_test.py::test_main_dispatches_phases_and_sequences_waves exercises wait_for_slot()/resource_headroom_ok(), which reads real /proc/loadavg via real_load1() and is never monkeypatched -- on this actual production Hetzner box (the same server this architecture runs many concurrent worker/supervisor processes on), a real load spike above CORES*0.90 (7.2) at test-run time would push affected issues into deferred_no_slot and make the test's routed_to_supervisor/redispatched assertions fail spuriously; the test should monkeypatch mod.resource_headroom_ok (or mod.real_load1) to remove this real-host-state dependency.

Both new test modules load the production scripts via importlib.util.spec_from_file_location, which executes their top-level `sys.path.insert(0, "/opt/veridian/scripts"); import dispatch_core`, so test collection itself depends on that absolute path existing on whatever machine runs pytest -- consistent with the existing codebase convention (not a new regression from this diff) but worth noting if these tests are ever expected to run somewhere other than this server.
